follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
oneTimers: $213M valuation allowance against deferred tax assets related to Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT) credits, recorded inside the $418M tax provision. The shareholder letter calls it out as the reason net income was flat year over year despite 10% revenue growth.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$167M: $180M of interest earned (Airbnb holds billions in guest payments before stays happen), minus $13M of other expense, mostly net foreign-exchange losses. Interest expense was immaterial, per the 10-Q.

segments.name: Stays & experiences
segments.note: Service fees charged to hosts and guests on every booking — Airbnb owns almost no property, so its revenue is a cut of each stay. One revenue stream.

takeaways.text: Nights and seats booked grew 9% — faster than last quarter — and gross booking value rose 14% to $22.9B as the average daily rate climbed 5% to $171. Growth was double-digit outside North America, and the new Reserve Now, Pay Later option helped bookings in the U.S.
takeaways.title: Bookings accelerated

takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA topped $2.0B for the first time in any quarter, a 50% margin. Airbnb collects guest money before the stay and owns no hotels, so growth converts unusually cleanly into profit and $1.3B of free cash flow.
takeaways.title: Record operating profit

takeaways.text: Net income of $1,374M was nearly unchanged from $1,368M a year ago. The tax provision included a $213M valuation allowance against tax credits related to the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax — without it, net income would have grown.
takeaways.title: A one-off tax charge held profit flat

verdict: Airbnb's biggest Q3 yet: 133.6 million nights and seats booked drove revenue up 10% to $4.1B, and net income held at $1.4B — 34 cents of every revenue dollar — despite a $213M one-off tax charge.
